punctuated:
允協，則有賢公卿輔翼大聖人之化焉。草茅賤士，其敢忘帝臣之願乎？謹對。

第二問
王應時

同考試官都給事中劉批：衆言淆亂，折諸聖，固有是言。今子論性，能析諸說之異，而歸諸力行之一言，子其希聖學而將有得者邪？

同考試官修撰秦批：性學一策，士千類能言之，求其於諸說異同剖析明允如此篇者，不多見也。豈區區記誦之學所能到邪？宜錄之。

考試官學士歐陽批：諸子不知性善，故其學起於意見。後世謂氣質有不善，欲不歸罪於習，而有以自諉。讀至此，令人深省。

考試官大學士張批：性學不明，以人之詳於言而畧於行故耳。此作能辨析諸家是非，而歸之力行之一言，始可與論性矣。錄之。

性貴盡也，非貴言也。其言之者，示人盡之
translation_en:
…in true concord, there will then be worthy dukes and ministers to assist the transforming influence of the great sage. How could a humble scholar from the countryside dare forget his aspiration to serve as the Emperor’s minister? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Wang Yingshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Chief Supervising Secretary: “When competing statements sow confusion, judge them by the sages”: this is indeed an established saying. In your discussion of human nature, you distinguish the differences among the various doctrines and bring them back to the single principle of diligent practice. Are you perhaps one who aspires to the learning of the sages and is about to attain insight into it?

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Senior Compiler: On a policy question concerning the study of human nature, scholars of a thousand kinds [?] can offer an account. Yet few essays can be found that analyze the agreements and differences among the various doctrines as lucidly and judiciously as this one. Could mere learning through memorization and recitation attain this? It should be included.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Academician: The various philosophers did not understand that human nature is good, and so their teachings arose from personal opinions. Later generations claimed that the psychophysical endowment contains elements that are not good, wishing to avoid placing the blame on acquired habits and thereby to give themselves an excuse. Reading this passage prompts deep reflection.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Grand Secretary: The study of human nature remains unclear simply because people are thorough in their words but cursory in their practice. This essay distinguishes what is right and wrong in the various schools and brings it back to the single principle of diligent practice. Only then can one discuss human nature with its author. Include it.

What matters is fully realizing one’s nature, not talking about it. Those who speak of it show people how to realize it fully…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
之功也言貴行也不貴辯也其辯之者欲
人行之無惑也盖人性本善而或梏之聖
人有憂焉於是言其所深造自得者牖人
心而反之善故其言非使人通曉辯說已
也欲其好學力行得之深而居之安故言
必可教教必可學學必可以成已成物而
徒言非所貴也盖嘗觀古之言性矣言乎
若性而有恒焉言乎節性而日邁焉言乎
率性以為道焉言乎誠善以盡性焉凡以
===
===
教力行也教慎習也盖聖人恒其性之中
矣欲夫人若焉而無敢戾致其性之和矣
欲夫人節焉而無敢縱盡其性之善矣欲
夫人率焉而無敢賊全其性之誠明矣欲
夫人思誠而無敢妄不戾不縱不賊不妄
而聲色臭味得其正喜怒哀樂中其節君
臣父子兄弟夫婦朋友盡其分習與性成
教之極功也道與時降勢以時異堯舜文
武之時教立於上而君師之道一道德齊

punctuated:
之功也。言貴行也，不貴辯也；其辯之者，欲人行之無惑也。盖人性本善，而或梏之，聖人有憂焉。於是言其所深造自得者，牖人心而反之善。故其言非使人通曉辯說已也，欲其好學力行，得之深而居之安。故言必可教，教必可學，學必可以成已成物，而徒言非所貴也。盖嘗觀古之言性矣：言乎若性而有恒焉，言乎節性而日邁焉，言乎率性以為道焉，言乎誠善以盡性焉，凡以教力行也，教慎習也。盖聖人恒其性之中矣，欲夫人若焉而無敢戾；致其性之和矣，欲夫人節焉而無敢縱；盡其性之善矣，欲夫人率焉而無敢賊；全其性之誠明矣，欲夫人思誠而無敢妄。不戾、不縱、不賊、不妄，而聲色臭味得其正，喜怒哀樂中其節，君臣、父子、兄弟、夫婦、朋友盡其分，習與性成，教之極功也。
道與時降，勢以時異。堯舜文武之時，教立於上，而君師之道一，道德齊
translation_en:
…the work of doing so. What is valued in words is putting them into practice, not disputation; those who argue their meaning do so because they want people to act without confusion. Human nature is originally good, yet things may shackle it, and the sages were troubled by this. They therefore spoke of what they had attained through profound study and grasped for themselves, opening people’s minds and restoring them to goodness. Their words were not intended merely to make people proficient in explanation and debate. They wanted people to love learning and strive to act, attaining a deep understanding and abiding securely in it. Thus, what is said must be capable of being taught; what is taught must be capable of being learned; and what is learned must enable one to perfect oneself and other beings. Mere words are not what is valued.
I have considered how the ancients spoke of human nature. They spoke of conforming to one’s nature and maintaining constancy; of regulating one’s nature and advancing daily; of following one’s nature as the Way; and of making goodness sincere so as fully to realize one’s nature. All this was to teach strenuous practice and care in forming habits. The sages maintained the equilibrium of their nature and wished everyone to conform to it, never daring to deviate. They brought their nature into harmony and wished everyone to exercise restraint, never daring to indulge themselves. They fully realized the goodness of their nature and wished everyone to follow it, never daring to injure it. They perfected their nature’s sincerity and understanding and wished everyone to strive for sincerity, never daring to be false. With no deviation, indulgence, injury, or falsehood, one’s responses to sounds, sights, smells, and tastes become proper; joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure attain their due measure; and rulers and ministers, fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, husbands and wives, and friends all fulfill their respective duties. Habit and nature develop together: this is the highest achievement of teaching.
The Way declined with the passage of time, and circumstances changed with the times. In the age of Yao, Shun, King Wen, and King Wu, teaching was established by those above, and the ways of ruler and teacher were one. They guided through virtue and brought order through…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
禮而人莫不敬應故行有枝葉言畧而功
倍孔子孟軻之時教立於下而君師之道
二百家殊方而人各為異說故詞有枝葉
言詳而功半蓋至於言詳而德行之教衰
意見之習盛於是人才風俗寖不逮古矣
嗟乎三代而下何其紛紛也孟子道性善
而羣喙競起衆言淆亂曰性惡者曰善惡
混者曰善惡各有定者曰無善無惡者各
是其是互相評譏其意則皆欲人為善易
===
惡者也而孟子闢之不遺餘力豈好為嘵
嘵者自今觀之孟子之言善也本之天命
徵之正情若曰能率其性斯無不善不可
反其性而為惡也諸子則或離情以為言
或雜習以為言若曰人當治其性以為善
不可以其性入於不善也故孟子之學順
理而無為也若决江河以注之海而無汎
濫焉雖困勉之功至於人十已千皆無為
而為性也非意也諸子之學刻意而有作

而羣喙競起衆言淆亂曰性惡者曰善惡
混者曰善惡各有定者曰無善無惡者各
是其是互相評譏其意則皆欲人爲善易
===
惡者也而孟子闢之不遺餘力豈好爲嘵
嘵者自今觀之孟子之言善也本之天命
徵之正情若曰能率其性斯無不善不可
反其性而爲惡也諸子則或離情以爲言
或雜習以爲言若曰人當治其性以爲善
不可以其性入於不善也故孟子之學順
理而無爲也若決江河以注之海而無汎
濫焉雖困勉之功至於人十己千皆無爲
而爲性也非意也諸子之學刻意而有作
punctuated:
禮，而人莫不敬應，故行有枝葉，言畧而功倍。孔子、孟軻之時，教立於下，而君師之道二，百家殊方，而人各為異說，故詞有枝葉，言詳而功半。蓋至於言詳，而德行之教衰，意見之習盛，於是人才風俗寖不逮古矣。
嗟乎！三代而下，何其紛紛也！孟子道性善，而羣喙競起，衆言淆亂。曰性惡者，曰善惡混者，曰善惡各有定者，曰無善無惡者，各是其是，互相評譏。其意則皆欲人為善易惡者也，而孟子闢之不遺餘力，豈好為嘵嘵者？自今觀之，孟子之言善也，本之天命，徵之正情，若曰能率其性，斯無不善，不可反其性而為惡也。諸子則或離情以為言，或雜習以為言，若曰人當治其性以為善，不可以其性入於不善也。故孟子之學，順理而無為也，若决江河以注之海，而無汎濫焉。雖困勉之功，至於人十已千，皆無為而為，性也，非意也。諸子之學，刻意而有作
translation_en:
…through ritual, and none failed to respond with reverence. Thus conduct branched out into its manifold expressions; words were few, yet their effect was doubled. In the time of Kongzi and Meng Ke, teaching was established among those below, and the roles of ruler and teacher became separate. The hundred schools pursued different approaches, and each person advanced a different doctrine. Thus words proliferated into branches and leaves; explanations were detailed, yet their effect was halved. Once explanations became elaborate, teaching through virtuous conduct declined, while the habit of advancing personal opinions flourished. Consequently, human talent and popular customs gradually fell short of antiquity.
Alas! How bewildering the profusion of doctrines since the Three Dynasties! Mengzi spoke of the goodness of human nature, and a multitude of voices arose in contention, their statements creating confusion. Some said that human nature was evil; some that good and evil were mingled in it; some that goodness and evil were each fixed; and some that it was neither good nor evil. Each affirmed the correctness of his own position, and they criticized and ridiculed one another. Their intention was in every case to have people do good and reform their evil ways. Yet Mengzi spared no effort in refuting them. Was he merely fond of noisy disputation? Viewed from the present, Mengzi’s account of goodness was rooted in Heaven’s mandate and verified through proper human feelings. It was as though he said: if people can follow their nature, they will be good in every respect; they must not go against their nature and do evil. The other thinkers either spoke of nature apart from feelings or mingled acquired habits into their accounts. It was as though they said: people must regulate their nature to become good and must not let their nature lead them into what is not good.
Thus Mengzi’s teaching follows principle without contrived action. It is like opening channels for the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers to flow into the sea without flooding. Even when the effort of persevering through difficulty reaches the point of doing a thousand times what others do ten times, it is still action without contrivance: it proceeds from nature, not deliberate intention. The teaching of the other thinkers strains intention and engages in contrived action…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
也若堤江河而鑿之道使無汎溢焉即功
力之熟至於不待思勉皆有作而成意也
非性也夫一陰一陽之道在天曰命命之
流行曰氣氣之凝聚曰質質之虛靈曰心
心之生理曰性性之發動曰情情之作止
反復曰習本末一原者也性者習之體習
者性之用性習而善惡分習與性成而善
惡不移始同終異者也故無不善者性之
常習而後有不善則逆其常者也然為善
===
斯慊不善斯不慊蓋根諸心而不可欺者
未始易乎其常孔子言性近習遠以至於
上智下愚此本末始終之别也孟子承之
謂善端為固有謂得之失之由於求舍謂
相倍蓰而無筭非才之罪此明其順逆常
變者也諸子則迷其本始故混其順逆而
以為皆其常然者以是為教而道人於善
其究也反害之矣何也意見作而天性賊
也夫楊朱無見於性之義則取為我以為

punctuated:
也。若堤江河而鑿之道，使無汎溢焉，即功力之熟至於不待思勉，皆有作而成，意也，非性也。夫一陰一陽之道，在天曰命，命之流行曰氣，氣之凝聚曰質，質之虛靈曰心，心之生理曰性，性之發動曰情，情之作止反復曰習，本末一原者也。性者，習之體；習者，性之用。性習而善惡分，習與性成而善惡不移，始同終異者也。故無不善者，性之常；習而後有不善，則逆其常者也。然為善斯慊，不善斯不慊，蓋根諸心而不可欺者，未始易乎其常。

孔子言性近習遠，以至於上智下愚，此本末始終之别也。孟子承之，謂善端為固有，謂得之失之由於求舍，謂相倍蓰而無筭，非才之罪，此明其順逆常變者也。諸子則迷其本始，故混其順逆，而以為皆其常然者。以是為教，而道人於善，其究也反害之矣。何也？意見作而天性賊也。夫楊朱無見於性之義，則取為我以為
translation_en:
…It is like embanking rivers and cutting channels for them so that they do not overflow. Even when one's efforts have become so practiced that neither thought nor exertion is required, the achievement still results from deliberate action: it belongs to intention, not to human nature. The Way of alternating yin and yang, in Heaven, is called the mandate; the flowing operation of the mandate is called vital energy (qi); the condensation of vital energy is called material constitution; the empty, numinous awareness of material constitution is called the mind; the life-giving principle of the mind is called human nature; the stirring of human nature is called feeling; and the repeated activity and repose of feeling are called habituation. Root and branches share a single source. Human nature is the substance of habituation; habituation is the functioning of human nature. As human nature undergoes habituation, good and evil diverge; once habit and nature have taken shape together, good and evil become fixed. Thus, what is the same at the outset differs in the end. To be entirely good is the constant condition of human nature; when evil arises through habituation, it runs counter to that constant condition. Yet doing good brings inner satisfaction, while doing evil brings dissatisfaction. What is rooted in the mind and cannot be deceived has never altered its constant condition.

Kongzi spoke of human natures being close to one another and habits drawing them far apart, extending this distinction to the supremely wise and the utterly foolish. This distinguishes root from branches and beginning from end. Mengzi carried this forward, saying that the beginnings of goodness are inherent, that gaining or losing them depends on seeking or abandoning them, and that people differ twofold, fivefold, and beyond calculation through no fault of their native capacities. This clarifies conformity and opposition to human nature, and its constancy and deviations. The other thinkers, however, lost sight of its root and beginning. They therefore confused conformity with opposition and regarded both as its constant condition. If they use this as their teaching and thereby guide people toward goodness, in the end they instead do harm. Why? Because contrived opinions arise and inborn nature is injured. Yang Zhu, failing to perceive the righteousness of human nature, took acting for oneself to be…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
義墨翟無見於性之仁則兼愛以為仁子
莫無見於性之中則執一以為中告子之
不動心鄉愿之徳許行之無為皆無見於
性之本故以其意見者為學而思以易天
下使天下皆能為為我之義兼愛之仁執
一之中猶未免為矯情鑿真况必不能為
也必不能為而又不知所為則恣情迷真
者仁義充塞中庸晦蝕而天下日入於亂
譬諸養生然黍稷稻粱其常也而必熊蹯
===
猩唇以充膳豈惟自伐天和将世之不能
皆得者有坐而甘餓或相食以斃耳至是
而後知諸說之紛紛不啻驅人於溺而率
之左衽而孟子之論所以距詖行正人心
者其為實用真足以比功禹周非無益之
空言也矣後人又推所未備將以輔行其
說乃以善歸性以不善歸氣質則信辯矣
然氣之冲和偏勝也質之剛柔明暗也本
天命之流行凝聚繼善而成性者也故曰

皆得者有坐而甘餓或相食以斃耳至是
而後知諸說之紛紛不啻驅人於溺而率
之左衽而孟子之論所以距詖行正人心
者其為實用真足以比功禹周非無益之
空言也矣後人又推所未備將以輔行其
說乃以善歸性以不善歸氣質則信辯矣
然氣之冲和偏勝也質之剛柔明暗也本
天命之流行凝聚繼善而成性者也故曰
punctuated:
義。墨翟無見於性之仁，則兼愛以為仁；子莫無見於性之中，則執一以為中。告子之不動心、鄉愿之徳、許行之無為，皆無見於性之本，故以其意見者為學，而思以易天下。使天下皆能為為我之義、兼愛之仁、執一之中，猶未免為矯情鑿真，况必不能為也。必不能為，而又不知所為，則恣情迷真者，仁義充塞，中庸晦蝕，而天下日入於亂。譬諸養生然，黍稷稻粱，其常也，而必熊蹯猩唇以充膳，豈惟自伐天和？将世之不能皆得者，有坐而甘餓，或相食以斃耳。至是而後知諸說之紛紛，不啻驅人於溺，而率之左衽；而孟子之論，所以距詖行、正人心者，其為實用，真足以比功禹周，非無益之空言也矣。

後人又推所未備，將以輔行其說，乃以善歸性，以不善歸氣質，則信辯矣。然氣之冲和偏勝也，質之剛柔明暗也，本天命之流行凝聚、繼善而成性者也。故曰：
translation_en:
…righteousness. Mo Di failed to perceive the benevolence inherent in human nature, and so took universal love to be benevolence; Zi Mo failed to perceive the mean inherent in human nature, and so took rigid adherence to one position to be the mean. Gaozi’s unmoved mind, the virtue of the village worthies, and Xu Xing’s nonaction all stemmed from a failure to perceive the root of human nature. Thus they made their own opinions the basis of learning and sought through them to transform the world. Even if everyone in the world could practice the righteousness of acting for oneself, the benevolence of universal love, and the mean of adhering to one position, these would still distort genuine feelings and mutilate what is authentic. How much worse, then, when people certainly cannot practice them! Unable to practice them, and unaware of what they should do, people indulge their feelings and lose sight of what is authentic; benevolence and righteousness are obstructed, the Mean is obscured and eroded, and the world sinks daily into disorder.

It is like nourishing life: millet, other varieties of millet, rice, and fine grain are the ordinary foods. If one insists instead on filling one’s table with bear paws and orangutan lips, does one merely impair one’s own natural harmony? Those in the world who cannot all obtain such things will sit idly and accept starvation, or devour one another and perish. Only at this point does one realize that these multitudinous doctrines amount to driving people to drown and leading them to fasten their robes on the left, in the manner of barbarians. Mencius’s arguments, by which he opposed deviant conduct [?] and rectified people’s minds, were truly of such practical benefit that their achievement can be compared with that of Yu and the Duke of Zhou. They were no useless, empty words.

Later thinkers further developed what had not been fully treated, intending to support and advance his teaching. They attributed goodness to human nature and evil to one’s psychophysical constitution: an eloquent distinction indeed. Yet whether vital energy is balanced and harmonious or disproportionately dominated by one tendency, and whether one’s constitution is firm or yielding, clear or dull, these are fundamentally the flowing and congealing of Heaven’s mandate, continuing goodness and bringing human nature into being. Thus it is said: …

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
性相近言其成性小異而皆善也有不善
則判然如寒暑晝夜不待習而已相遠矣
故不善者習之所成非氣質之本然孟子
所謂弗思弗求者也故人不可不慎其所
習習於善雖柔且暗善也習為不善雖剛
且明不善也故困而不學者然後為下中
人以下不可語上者未嘗不可使由之也
後世徒見自幼而惡者疑非習所成而又
不可以汚性則推之於性習之間曰此氣
===
質也云爾蓋徒知視聽言動之習而未知
不視聽言動之習也知有心之習而未知
無心之習也居養之移氣體胎有教而子
多才此其漸習豈以心思耳目哉知胎之
教與居養之移漸染之習則自幼而惡者
皆成於習而非天賦之一定故無不可反
而之善者士之自成自道無所可諉矣若
曰氣質所成也則言非禮義與自謂不能
者且諉於天之困之而堅其自暴自棄之

punctuated: 「性相近」，言其成性小異而皆善也。有不善，則判然如寒暑晝夜，不待習而已相遠矣。故不善者，習之所成，非氣質之本然，孟子所謂「弗思弗求」者也。故人不可不慎其所習。習於善，雖柔且暗，善也；習為不善，雖剛且明，不善也。故困而不學者，然後為下。「中人以下，不可語上」者，未嘗不可使由之也。後世徒見自幼而惡者，疑非習所成，而又不可以汚性，則推之於性習之間，曰：「此氣質也。」云爾。蓋徒知視聽言動之習，而未知不視聽言動之習也；知有心之習，而未知無心之習也。居養之移氣體，胎有教而子多才，此其漸習，豈以心思耳目哉？知胎之教與居養之移、漸染之習，則自幼而惡者，皆成於習，而非天賦之一定，故無不可反而之善者。士之自成自道，無所可諉矣。若曰氣質所成也，則言非禮義與自謂不能者，且諉於天之困之，而堅其自暴自棄之
translation_en:
…“By nature, people are close to one another”: this means that their constituted natures differ slightly but are all good. If there were evil in them, they would be as sharply distinguished as cold and heat, day and night; they would already be far apart without waiting for habituation. Thus, what is not good is produced by habituation, rather than belonging to the original condition of one’s psychophysical constitution. It is what Mencius meant by “failing to reflect and failing to seek.” People therefore must take care over what they become accustomed to. Those habituated to goodness are good, even if yielding and dull; those habituated to wrongdoing are not good, even if firm and intelligent. Thus, only those who encounter difficulty yet fail to learn belong to the lowest class. As for those of whom it is said, “One cannot speak of higher things to people below average,” it has never been impossible to have them follow the Way.

Later generations merely observed people who were bad from childhood and doubted that habituation had made them so. Yet, unwilling to sully human nature, they assigned the cause to something between nature and habituation, saying simply, “This is their psychophysical constitution.” They knew only of habituation through seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, without knowing of habituation apart from these activities. They knew of conscious habituation without knowing of unconscious habituation. One’s station and nurture transform one’s bearing and body; instruction during gestation produces children of many abilities. Does such gradual habituation depend upon conscious thought, ears, or eyes? Once one understands prenatal instruction, the transformations wrought by station and nurture, and habituation through gradual influence, one sees that those who are bad from childhood have all been made so by habituation: their condition is not immutably fixed by Heaven’s endowment. Thus, none is incapable of returning to goodness. In perfecting and guiding themselves, scholars have nothing on which to shift responsibility.

If, however, one says that this condition is produced by psychophysical constitution, then those whose speech rejects ritual propriety and righteousness, and those who declare themselves incapable, will shift responsibility onto Heaven for having constrained them, and harden their disposition toward doing violence to themselves and abandoning themselves…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
心又何教之立哉今孔孟之教如日中天
而紛紛者不得行矣明問猶反復辯詰豈
非示承學以不謬所從且使出乎其所習
以見諸實用而不為徒言矣乎愚也何敢
以自賊也
第三問
劉珝
同考試官右給事中何批馬政積久弊滋更宜通
變而振厲之子能條析利害審畫允衷可謂經
===
時之畧誠行子說必底成績無疑也
同考試官檢討毛批酌兵民之害講飼牧
之跡馬政之大者執此以往又何弊焉宜錄之
同考試官修撰黄批馬之政兹極弊大壞之
時子能詳考其故亟欲通變以宜民篇終及於牧政
論尤探治之本也經國忠懇辭足以發之是可為
承平獻也
同考試官侍講邢批馬政備邊急務子能
達古今之故究利病之原而處置得宜足為司牧

同考試官修撰黄　批〔馬之政茲極弊矣讀之時子能詳考其故亟欲通變以宜民籥綜及民牧政〕
論尤探治之本也經國忠懇辭足以發之是可爲
同考試官侍講邢　批〔馬政備悉忠務子能達古今之故究利病之原□□□□□□□是爲司牧〕
承平獻也
punctuated:
心，又何教之立哉？今孔孟之教如日中天，而紛紛者不得行矣。明問猶反復辯詰，豈非示承學以不謬所從，且使出乎其所習，以見諸實用，而不為徒言矣乎？愚也何敢以自賊也！

第三問
劉珝

同考試官右給事中何批：馬政積久弊滋，更宜通變而振厲之。子能條析利害，審畫允衷，可謂經時之畧。誠行子說，必底成績，無疑也。

同考試官檢討毛批：酌兵民之害，講飼牧之跡，馬政之大者。執此以往，又何弊焉？宜錄之。

同考試官修撰黄批：馬之政，兹極弊大壞之時。子能詳考其故，亟欲通變以宜民。篇終及於牧政，論尤探治之本也。經國忠懇，辭足以發之，是可為承平獻也。

同考試官侍講邢批：馬政，備邊急務。子能達古今之故，究利病之原，而處置得宜，足為司牧
translation_en:
…such a disposition—how, then, could any teaching be established? Now the teachings of Confucius and Mencius shine like the sun at its zenith, and the competing doctrines can gain no currency. Yet your discerning question repeatedly examines and challenges the matter. Is this not to show students how to avoid error in what they follow, and also to lead them beyond their accustomed learning into practical application, so that it does not remain mere words? Ignorant though I am, how would I dare thus to injure myself!

Third Policy Question
Liu Xu 劉珝

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Right Supervising Secretary: Abuses in horse administration have multiplied over time; it is all the more necessary to adapt its methods and restore its vigor. You analyze the benefits and harms systematically, and your carefully considered plans strike the proper balance. This may be called a strategy for addressing the affairs of the age. If your proposals were truly implemented, they would assuredly produce results.

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Examining Editor: Weighing the harms borne by soldiers and commoners and examining the practices of feeding and pasturing horses are the major concerns of horse administration. If these principles are followed, what abuses could remain? This essay deserves inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Senior Compiler: Horse administration has now reached a state of extreme abuse and grave collapse. You examine its causes in detail and urgently seek adaptations that will benefit the people. At the essay’s conclusion you turn to pasturage administration, and your argument probes still more deeply into the foundations of good governance. Your language adequately expresses your loyal earnestness in ordering the state. This can serve as a contribution to an age of peace.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xing, Expositor: Horse administration is an urgent task in preparing the frontier defenses. You comprehend the circumstances of past and present, investigate the sources of benefits and harms, and propose appropriate measures. Your essay can serve as a guide for those charged with horse administration…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
者鑒不特式多士而已
考試官學士歐陽批馬蕃固急務民瘠尤非
細故手之言不徒捄偏補敝盖深探其本矣殆
亦秉心塞淵者
考試官大學士張批馬政最今日備邊急務此
作獨能詳言其弊之所由而經處之鑿鑿可行
殆究心於世務者取之
善立法者周天下之慮者也善捄敝者相
天下之時者也夫法之立其初未嘗不善
===
而時之所趨不得不救人情非至於臨利
害更事變則襲於所安坐觀其敝而不為
之所故知者起福於無形銷患於未萌苟
可以強國不法其故苟可以利民不拘其
俗通變不窮應用不忒然後可以有制於
天下明此可與語政矣夫周官以戎政隷
於司馬而馬之政其用大矣昔周盛時因
井田以制軍賦井邑丘甸出戎馬四匹積
而至於畿方千里則天子馬四萬諸侯邦

punctuated:
者鑒，不特式多士而已。
考試官學士歐陽批：馬蕃固急務，民瘠尤非細故。手之言不徒捄偏補敝，盖深探其本矣，殆亦秉心塞淵者。
考試官大學士張批：馬政最今日備邊急務。此作獨能詳言其弊之所由，而經處之，鑿鑿可行，殆究心於世務者，取之。
善立法者，周天下之慮者也；善捄敝者，相天下之時者也。夫法之立，其初未嘗不善，而時之所趨，不得不救。人情非至於臨利害、更事變，則襲於所安，坐觀其敝，而不為之所。故知者起福於無形，銷患於未萌。苟可以強國，不法其故；苟可以利民，不拘其俗。通變不窮，應用不忒，然後可以有制於天下。明此，可與語政矣。夫《周官》以戎政隷於司馬，而馬之政，其用大矣。昔周盛時，因井田以制軍賦，井邑丘甸出戎馬四匹，積而至於畿方千里，則天子馬四萬，諸侯邦
translation_en:
…a mirror for those charged with governing, and not merely a model for the examination candidates.
Examiner Ouyang, Academician, comments: Increasing the horse population is certainly urgent, but the impoverishment of the people is still less a trivial matter. Your words [?] do more than correct imbalances and remedy abuses: they probe deeply into the root of the matter. You too seem to be a person of steadfast and profound purpose.
Examiner Zhang, Grand Secretary, comments: Horse administration is today a most urgent matter for frontier defense. This composition is exceptional in explaining in detail the causes of its abuses and proposing measures to address them that are demonstrably practicable. Its author appears to have devoted serious thought to the affairs of the age. Accept it.
Those skilled at establishing laws consider comprehensively the concerns of all under Heaven; those skilled at remedying abuses assess the circumstances of their age throughout the realm. When laws are first established, they are invariably well intended; yet the direction in which circumstances develop makes remedial action unavoidable. Human nature is such that, unless people confront benefit and harm and experience changing affairs, they persist in what they find comfortable, sitting by and watching abuses without taking measures to address them. Thus the wise bring forth blessings before they have taken shape and dispel troubles before they sprout. If a measure can strengthen the state, they need not model it on old practices; if it can benefit the people, they need not be constrained by prevailing customs. Only when they adapt to change without exhaustion and respond to practical needs without error can they bring order to all under Heaven. With someone who understands this, one may discuss government.
The Offices of Zhou places military administration under the Minister of War, and the administration of horses is of great practical importance. Formerly, when the Zhou flourished, military levies were regulated on the basis of the well-field system. The units of jing, yi, qiu, and dian supplied four warhorses [per dian]. Reckoned across the royal domain, a thousand li square, this gave the Son of Heaven forty thousand horses. As for the domains of the feudal lords…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
國大夫采地由此其數可考巳四時有祭
祭各有義春馬祖言天駟也夏先牧言始
飼者秋馬社言始乘者冬馬步懼為災也
校人廋人圉師圉牧趣馬巫馬皆所以攻
執簡習以調其性而蕃其生也由此其政
可考巳栢翳諳鳥獸之情而畜馬息故帝
堯氏之以嬴得世其官非子牧汧渭之間
而大有功故周孝王邑之以秦不廢其業
漢初自天子不能具純駟傳至武帝富庶
===
阡陌成羣及匈奴入塞征伐四出衛青擊
胡李廣利擊大宛其後乃發酒泉橐駝負
食出玉門輪臺之詔始令郡國二千石各
上畜馬方畧馬一匹復卒三人貞觀時張
萬歲總領羣牧鳩括殘騎徙之隴右至麟
德垂四十年而疋縑可易自是而毛仲牧
之雲錦成羣突厥欵塞長興時范延光奏
陳方患官馬太多糜費國力至清泰曾幾
何年即令牝牡但勝衣甲並行印記後唐

祭各有義春馬祖言天駟也夏先牧言始
飼者秋馬社言始乘者冬馬步懼為災也
校人庾人圉師圉牧趣馬巫馬皆所以攻
執簡習以調其性而蕃其生也由此其故
可考已極賢諸鳥獸之情而畜馬息故帝
堯氏之以嬴得世其官非子牧汧渭之間
而大有功故周孝王邑之以秦不廢其業
漢初自天子不能具鈞駟傳至武帝富庶
===
阡陌成羣及匈奴入塞征伐四出衛青擊
胡李廣剎擊大宛其後乃發酒泉橐駝負
食出玉門輪臺之詔始令郡國二千石各
上畜馬方畧馬一匹復卒三人貞觀時張
萬歲總領羣牧鳩括殘燼徙之隴右至麟
德垂四十年而道繼可易自是而毛仲牧
之雲錦成羣突厥款塞長興時范延光奏
陳方患官馬太多糜費國力至清泰曾幾
何年即令札牲但勝衣甲並行印記後唐
punctuated: 國、大夫采地，由此其數可考巳。四時有祭，祭各有義：春馬祖，言天駟也；夏先牧，言始飼者；秋馬社，言始乘者；冬馬步，懼為災也。校人、廋人、圉師、圉牧、趣馬、巫馬，皆所以攻執簡習，以調其性而蕃其生也。由此其政可考巳。栢翳諳鳥獸之情，而畜馬息，故帝堯氏之以嬴，得世其官；非子牧汧渭之間，而大有功，故周孝王邑之以秦，不廢其業。漢初，自天子不能具純駟，傳至武帝，富庶，阡陌成羣。及匈奴入塞，征伐四出，衛青擊胡，李廣利擊大宛，其後乃發酒泉橐駝負食出玉門。輪臺之詔，始令郡國二千石各上畜馬方畧，馬一匹復卒三人。貞觀時，張萬歲總領羣牧，鳩括殘騎，徙之隴右，至麟德，垂四十年，而疋縑可易。自是而毛仲牧之，雲錦成羣，突厥欵塞。長興時，范延光奏陳，方患官馬太多，糜費國力；至清泰，曾幾何年，即令牝牡但勝衣甲，並行印記。後唐
translation_en:
…states and the appanages of grand officers: their numbers of horses can be ascertained from this. Sacrifices were offered in all four seasons, each with its own significance. In spring, sacrifice to the Horse Ancestor referred to the celestial team of four horses; in summer, sacrifice to the First Herdsman referred to the first person to feed horses; in autumn, sacrifice to the Horse Shrine referred to the first person to ride them; in winter, sacrifice to the Horse Pestilence Spirit expressed fear that it might cause calamity. The directors of horses, stable officers, chief grooms, horse keepers, equerries, and horse shamans all served to handle, select, and train the horses, taming their dispositions and increasing their numbers. From this, too, the administration of horses can be ascertained.

Boyi understood the nature of birds and beasts, and the horses he raised multiplied. Emperor Yao therefore bestowed on him the surname Ying, and he was able to transmit his office hereditarily. Feizi tended horses between the Qian and Wei rivers and achieved great success. King Xiao of Zhou therefore granted him a fief at Qin, allowing his work to continue.

At the beginning of the Han, even the Son of Heaven could not assemble a team of four horses of a single color. By the reign of Emperor Wu, prosperity and abundance had grown, and herds filled the paths between the fields. When the Xiongnu entered the frontier, military expeditions went out in every direction: Wei Qing attacked the Hu, and Li Guangli attacked Dayuan. Subsequently, camels were dispatched from Jiuquan to carry provisions beyond Yumen Pass. Only with the Luntai edict were the officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank in the commanderies and kingdoms ordered to submit plans for raising horses, with three men exempted from military service for each horse supplied.

During the Zhenguan era, Zhang Wansui took overall charge of the state herds, gathered the remaining cavalry horses, and moved them to Longyou. By the Linde era, nearly forty years later, a horse could be bought for a bolt of silk. Thereafter Maozhong tended them, and the herds resembled clouds of brocade; the Tujue came to the frontier to offer submission. During the Changxing era, Fan Yanguang submitted a memorial reporting that the concern at the time was an excess of government horses, which consumed the state's resources. Yet by the Qingtai era—how few years later!—an order was issued that mares and stallions alike should be branded for service so long as they could bear an armored rider. The Later Tang…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
之業日以不振夫畜牧繁而邦家實內治
寧而外攘舉不然銳志四夷者乃罷中國
之人勤心遠畧者多忽目前之虞馬之政
所係豈其微哉惟
皇祖驅斥胡元削平僭亂首命劉惟謙申明馬
政嚴督所司盡心芻牧務底蕃息有不如
令者罪之今內之
天子十二閑外之南北太僕直隸河南山東所
轄之地或計丁稅而使之牧或進駒而備
===
用或點驗而俵散其陝西山西遼東甘肅
四川或設苑監而牧之于官或以茶縑而
市之於夷皆酌古用中而為裕用禦侮之
道者也然法久則弊滋時極則政通夫官
散馬於編氓計丁度畝立之羣長歲課所
出之駒生則籍記斃則償直分日而飼需
次而輸間或駑駘末品不適於用轉徙流
易必足其數未俵則愛之若子既俵則置
若棄民之牧之若秦人為越人牧羊然

市之於夷皆酌古用中而為裕國禦侮之
道者也然法久則弊滋時屢則致通夫官

若棄民之牧之若秦人為越人牧羊然
punctuated:
之業日以不振。夫畜牧繁而邦家實，內治寧而外攘舉。不然，銳志四夷者乃罷中國之人，勤心遠畧者多忽目前之虞。馬之政所係豈其微哉！惟皇祖驅斥胡元，削平僭亂，首命劉惟謙申明馬政，嚴督所司，盡心芻牧，務底蕃息，有不如令者罪之。今內之天子十二閑，外之南北太僕、直隸、河南、山東所轄之地，或計丁稅而使之牧，或進駒而備用，或點驗而俵散。其陝西、山西、遼東、甘肅、四川，或設苑監而牧之于官，或以茶縑而市之於夷，皆酌古用中而為裕用禦侮之道者也。
然法久則弊滋，時極則政通。夫官散馬於編氓，計丁度畝，立之羣長，歲課所出之駒，生則籍記，斃則償直，分日而飼，需次而輸。間或駑駘末品，不適於用，轉徙流易，必足其數。未俵則愛之若子，既俵則置若棄。民之牧之，若秦人為越人牧羊然。
translation_en:
…the fortunes of the Later Tang declined day by day. When livestock multiply, the state becomes well supplied; when internal government is peaceful, efforts to repel external enemies can proceed. Otherwise, those intent on attacking the peoples of the four quarters merely exhaust the people of the Central Realm, while those preoccupied with distant strategies often neglect dangers close at hand. Can the matters bound up with horse administration be considered insignificant?
When our imperial ancestor drove out the alien Yuan and subdued usurpers and rebels, he first ordered Liu Weiqian to clarify the regulations governing horse administration and strictly supervise the responsible officials. They were to devote themselves to feeding and pasturing the horses, ensuring that they multiplied; anyone who failed to comply with the orders was punished. Today, within the capital there are the Son of Heaven’s twelve stables; outside it, in the territories under the jurisdiction of the Courts of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing and Beijing, and in Zhili, Henan, and Shandong, people are variously assigned horse-rearing duties according to assessments on adult males, required to present colts for service, or allotted horses following inspection. In Shaanxi, Shanxi, Liaodong, Gansu, and Sichuan, either imperial horse-pasture offices are established to rear horses under official management, or tea and silk are exchanged for horses from non-Chinese peoples. All these arrangements draw judiciously on antiquity and adopt appropriate measures to ensure ample supplies and resist aggression.
Yet as regulations endure, abuses proliferate; when circumstances reach an extremity, administration adapts. Officials distribute horses among registered commoners, assess their adult males and acreage, appoint herd headmen over them, and annually exact a quota of the colts produced. Births are entered in registers, while deaths require reimbursement of the horses’ value. Feeding duties are allotted by day, and horses are delivered in turn. Sometimes inferior, worn-out horses are unfit for service; they are moved about and exchanged, but the prescribed number must always be made up. Before allotment, they are cherished like children; after allotment, they are left as though abandoned. The commoners tend them as a man of Qin might tend sheep for a man of Yue.

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
給軍騎操官出芻秣豪家私門假以驅馳
瘠損羸弱坐視其斃況望其亭亭蕃且孳
哉深春牧放及秋乃歸今假是以削其芻
秣名存實亡則軍士重為馬困也縱嚴補
亡之禁將何裨哉議者謂營軍騎操故有
苑監今半已湮沒宜亟為清理復古行之
九關豐曠之野官備芻飼列廄大鑊攢槽
合食羣長時為之添杚求良教駣攻駒將
領以葺其政士卒為之分直仍
===
勅憲臣董其事以時廉視嚴班政之數重侵冒
之禁一卒一騎用則駕鞍閒則休息人與
馬而俱利者也雖欲私其用不可得也牧
之民者其害也甚矣內郡有司莫若約其
丁稅所出而歸之于官官為之擇地立羣
長以牧之則責其專職而久其成功欲馬
之無蕃不可得也遠郡水旱則折變綠納
以貯太盈或每歲銀馬中半此固人情所
樂從者官與民而俱益者也否則視宋之

九關豐曠之野官備芻飼列廐大鏤攢槽
合食羣長時為之游牝求良教駣攻駒將
領以董其政士卒為之分直仍
===
勑憲臣董其事以時廉視嚴班政之數重侵冒
之禁一卒一騎用則駕轂閒則休息人與
馬而俱利者也雖欲私其用不可得也牧
之民者其害也甚矣內郡有司莫若約其
丁稅所出而歸之于官官為之擇地立羣
長以牧之則責其專職而久其成功欲馬
之繁蕃不可得也遠郡水旱則折變緣納
以貯大盈或每歲銀馬中半此固人情所
樂從者官與民而俱益者也否則視宋之

給軍騎操，官出芻秣，豪家私門假以驅馳，瘠損羸弱，坐視其斃，況望其亭亭蕃且孳哉？深春牧放，及秋乃歸。今假是以削其芻秣，名存實亡，則軍士重為馬困也。縱嚴補亡之禁，將何裨哉？議者謂營軍騎操，故有苑監，今半已湮沒，宜亟為清理，復古行之。九關豐曠之野，官備芻飼，列廄大鑊，攢槽合食，羣長時為之添杚，求良教駣攻駒，將領以葺其政，士卒為之分直，仍勅憲臣董其事，以時廉視，嚴班政之數，重侵冒之禁。一卒一騎，用則駕鞍，閒則休息，人與馬而俱利者也。雖欲私其用，不可得也。
牧之民者，其害也甚矣。內郡有司莫若約其丁稅所出，而歸之于官，官為之擇地，立羣長以牧之，則責其專職，而久其成功，欲馬之無蕃，不可得也。遠郡水旱，則折變綠納，以貯太盈，或每歲銀馬中半，此固人情所樂從者，官與民而俱益者也。否則視宋之
translation_en:
…When horses are supplied to the troops for mounted drill, the government provides their fodder and grain, but powerful households borrow them for their own riding and driving. They let the horses grow emaciated and weak, then stand by and watch them die. How could one expect the horses to grow tall and vigorous, flourish, and breed? In late spring they are put out to pasture and return only in autumn. Now this practice is used as a pretext to cut their fodder and grain: the provision survives in name but has vanished in substance, and soldiers suffer still further burdens on account of the horses. Even strict enforcement of the requirement to replace losses would do what good? Those discussing the matter say that pasture directorates formerly existed to support mounted drill among garrison troops. Half have now disappeared; they should urgently be investigated and restored, reviving the ancient practice. In the fertile, open country of the nine passes, the government should provide fodder, set out stables and large cauldrons, and group feeding troughs together for communal feeding. Herd chiefs should replenish the feed from time to time [?], seek out good horses, and train the young horses and colts. Commanders should put the administration in order, and soldiers should divide the duty shifts among themselves. Censorial officials should also be commanded to oversee these affairs and conduct timely inspections, strictly enforcing the prescribed allocations [?] and prohibitions against misappropriation and fraudulent claims. Each soldier would have one mount: when needed, it would be saddled; when idle, it would rest. Both men and horses would benefit. Even anyone wishing to divert them to private use would find it impossible.
Entrusting their rearing to the common people does very great harm. In the interior prefectures, the responsible officials would do best to assess the proceeds of the poll levy and turn them over to the government. The government should select pastureland and appoint herd chiefs to rear the horses, holding them responsible for this particular duty and allowing sufficient time for their work to succeed. It would then be impossible for the horses not to flourish. If distant prefectures suffer floods or drought, their obligations should be commuted and remitted [?], to be stored in the “Great Surplus” [?]; alternatively, each year's payment could be half in silver and half in horses. This is certainly something people would willingly accept, benefiting officials and commoners alike. Otherwise, compared with the Song dynasty's …

…is even more burdensome than the Song horse-keeping system. Under that system, households received exemptions from other service obligations; now those obligations remain. How can the people endure this? At the frontier pasture directorates, land fit for cultivation should be made into agricultural garrisons. Where it cannot be cultivated but the water is sweet and the grass tender, strict prohibitions should be reaffirmed and breeding expanded. When an alarm arises along the frontier, there will naturally be enough horses available for defense. Moreover, the exchanges of tea and salt for horses supply the major garrisons and replenish the directorates’ herds. The regulations are exceedingly comprehensive.

Formerly, Emperor Xiaozong accepted proposals from court deliberations and specially appointed a senior censorial official to supervise horse administration. For a time, horses were plentiful and the state strong; the northern invaders dared not turn southward to encroach upon us. In recent years, frontier officials have repeatedly reported shortages, and our ministry has from time to time supplied funds for purchases in separate markets. Why has this happened? Formerly, officials responsible for horses … their duties [?]; now these offices have all become places for cultivating reputations and securing promotion in rank. How far this is from the duties performed by Boyi and Feizi!

If the benefit is not tenfold, one should not change an undertaking; if plans are not clarified early, one cannot attempt great things; if supplies are not prepared beforehand, one cannot meet sudden emergencies; if administration does not make a fresh start, one cannot enjoy success. The Book of Odes says: “Holding his heart sincere and profound, he had three thousand horses and mares [?].” It also says: “His thoughts know no bounds; thinking of his horses, he makes them fine.” The horses of Duke Xi and Duke Wen were indeed numerous, yet when the poets sang in praise of this achievement, they traced it to the heart. Did they not understand the Way?

Those who now shepherd the people deceive their superiors and pursue private interests. Their people’s hunger and thirst do not trouble their thoughts, and whether the people are well nourished or emaciated is no pressing personal concern. The emperor’s abundant benevolence is dammed up and cannot flow; the common people’s complaints are obstructed and cannot reach those above. Thus …

translation_en:
…few provide benevolent nurture as fathers and mothers. Prefects and magistrates are shepherds of the people; when the right men hold these posts, the people find protection in them. Thus, what is rooted in their hearts must be compassionate love; what is promulgated in their commands must be loyal and beneficial instruction; and what wins the people's trust must be good and conscientious government. Moving with the times, they must leave no benefit undeveloped; seeking security for the people, they must leave no harm unremoved. Otherwise, what use is a shepherd?
Cui Shi of the Han wrote in his Discourse on Government: “For several generations, government has abounded in indulgence and leniency. The driver lets fall his reins; the horses slacken their bits. Fan Ye admired these words, judging them to show a clear understanding of the essentials of government. Once this is understood, the urgent tasks of today plainly extend beyond the administration of horses. If you, honored sir, should approve and advance this argument, there are still deeper matters that may be offered to this enlightened age.

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
宋儒學之得失而折衷之蓋潜心儒者之實而
有得者錄以為務名者戒

學之失其有志於古之儒邪

發問之意正欲占士子嚮往之志而期之用耳觀
子所言則其中可知矣他日有以儒名世者必子

===

而弗學不可以言儒其效于用猶穡之資
食也器之資用也仕而弗效不可以言學
故仕所以行夫學也學所以豫夫仕也存
之為德行而藏器以待時措之為事業而
行義以達道此儒之所以為儒也若夫博
物洽聞以為學其失也不足以語心得之
精推之于用必不達程能計功以為政其
失也不足以語靖共之義投之以艱必不

…the merits and failings of Song Confucian learning and reaches a balanced judgment upon them. He has evidently devoted himself to the substance of Confucian learning and gained insight into it. This answer is recorded as an admonition to those who pursue reputation.
Examiner Academician Ouyang comments: Confucians embody the Way and are therefore able to put their learning into practice. If they merely transmit the Classics and study literary composition, what benefit does this bring to practical affairs? You deplore the failings of Han and Tang Confucian learning; surely you aspire to be a Confucian of the ancient kind?
Examiner Grand Secretary Zhang comments: Confucian learning is valued for its practical application. The intention in posing this question was precisely to discern the aspirations of the examination candidates and to look forward to their putting their learning to use. From what you say, your inner convictions can be known. If anyone in days to come wins renown as a Confucian, it will surely be you!
For a Confucian, learning is like plowing for a farmer or skilled workmanship for an artisan. A Confucian who does not learn cannot be called a Confucian. The practical results of his learning are like the food supplied by crops or the usefulness supplied by implements. One who serves in office without producing results cannot be said to have learned. Thus, service in office is the means of putting learning into practice, and learning is the means of preparing for service. Preserved within oneself, it becomes virtuous conduct: one keeps one's abilities in reserve and awaits the proper time. Applied to affairs, it becomes achievement: one practices righteousness to realize the Way. This is what makes a Confucian a Confucian. As for taking wide knowledge of things and extensive information to constitute learning, its failing is that it falls short of the refinement of understanding attained in the heart; applied to practical affairs, it will surely prove ineffective. 于所遇不得以自效于其時則亦末如之

天地位萬物育故曰篤恭而天下平斯則
儒者功用之全也使政而不本於學是之
謂無體即顯設於事功要之終詭於道也
况其否者乎學而不達于政是之謂無用
即窮徹於幽深要之無補于世也况其否
者乎惟夫唐虞三代之際自朝廷以至海
隅自天子以至庶人莫不知學精一執中
punctuated: 濟。曾是而可以為儒乎？若夫有其具而厄于所遇，不得以自效于其時，則亦末如之何也已。知此，則漢唐宋諸儒所學之是非、史臣紀載之得失，可得而論已。愚也盖嘗宗孔氏，服儒行，而得其槩。請先終其物，而後及于諸儒，可乎？孔子之言儒也，盖曰：「其自立也固，其備豫也素，其特立也介，剛毅而不邁，仕而不溺，舉賢援能，任舉而不私，不隕穫于貧賤，不充詘于富貴。」由此言之，是其學也，以求道也，而仕之具以立；其政也，以達道也，而學之素以行。故曰：「致中和，天地位，萬物育。」故曰：「篤恭而天下平。」斯則儒者功用之全也。使政而不本於學，是之謂無體，即顯設於事功，要之終詭於道也，況其否者乎？學而不達于政，是之謂無用，即窮徹於幽深，要之無補于世也，況其否者乎？惟夫唐虞三代之際，自朝廷以至海隅，自天子以至庶人，莫不知學，精一執中
translation_en: …succeed. Can someone like this really be called a Confucian scholar? As for one who possesses the requisite capacities but is constrained by his circumstances and cannot put them to use in his own time, there is simply nothing to be done. Once this is understood, we can discuss the rights and wrongs of the learning of Confucian scholars of the Han, Tang, and Song, and the merits and faults of the historians’ accounts. In my humble way, I have followed Confucius, practiced Confucian conduct, and gained a general understanding of it. May I first complete my account of its substance [?], and then turn to the various scholars? Speaking of the Confucian scholar, Confucius said: “He is firm in establishing himself, makes his preparations well in advance, and stands alone with integrity. He is resolute without being overbearing, and holds office without being corrupted by it. He recommends the worthy and assists the capable, taking responsibility for his recommendations without favoritism. He is neither disheartened by poverty and low station nor puffed up or bent from his principles by wealth and high rank.” From this we may say that his learning seeks the Way and thereby establishes his qualifications for office; his government puts the Way into effect and thereby brings his long-cultivated learning into practice. Thus it is said: “Bring centrality and harmony to their fullest realization, and Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things flourish.” And again: “Through profound reverence, all under Heaven is brought to peace.” This is the full scope of the Confucian scholar’s achievement and usefulness. To govern without a foundation in learning is to lack substance. Even if one achieves conspicuous practical results, these will ultimately deviate from the Way; how much more so when one fails! To pursue learning without bringing it to bear on government is to lack practical use. Even if one penetrates the most profound mysteries, this ultimately does nothing to benefit the world; how much more so when one fails! In the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, from the court to the remotest shores, from the Son of Heaven to the common people, none were ignorant of learning. The teaching of being discerning and single-minded and holding fast to the mean…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
之㫖授受於君臣之間而萬世心學之源
以肇昭明熈皥之化所由出也嗣是伊傅
周召之為臣與一時服休服采之士亦罔
匪賢哲而治得與唐虞並稱也又奚疑哉
當是時也其布列有位莫非儒也故儒之
名不著迨周道日衰學術棼裂儒者之澤
漸湮于天下孔子不得已而鳴其道於齊
魯之間其於儒三致意焉而儒之名始彰
觀其所以告哀公者可知矣然竟不得一
===
試而止秦坑漢嫚之後世顧以儒相訾而
儒之名亦索然泯矣幸而中弛挾書之法
又有臨雍拜老如明帝者以作于後天下
始知慕儒而問學然儒者之實則自是判
然與古異故自漢而下史臣始别為傳述
焉兩漢有儒林傳所載如丁寬牟融輩可
考而知也唐更為儒學傳所載如徐文遠
輩可考而知也宋因漢為儒林傳自聶崇
義而下又可考而知也夫固彬彬焉盛矣

punctuated: 之㫖，授受於君臣之間，而萬世心學之源以肇，昭明熈皥之化所由出也。嗣是伊傅周召之為臣，與一時服休服采之士，亦罔匪賢哲，而治得與唐虞並稱也，又奚疑哉？當是時也，其布列有位莫非儒也，故儒之名不著。迨周道日衰，學術棼裂，儒者之澤漸湮于天下，孔子不得已而鳴其道於齊魯之間。其於儒三致意焉，而儒之名始彰，觀其所以告哀公者可知矣。然竟不得一試而止。秦坑漢嫚之後，世顧以儒相訾，而儒之名亦索然泯矣。幸而中弛挾書之法，又有臨雍拜老如明帝者以作于後，天下始知慕儒而問學。然儒者之實，則自是判然與古異。故自漢而下，史臣始别為傳述焉。兩漢有《儒林傳》，所載如丁寬、牟融輩，可考而知也。唐更為《儒學傳》，所載如徐文遠輩，可考而知也。宋因漢為《儒林傳》，自聶崇義而下，又可考而知也。夫固彬彬焉盛矣。
translation_en:
…the purport of these teachings was transmitted between ruler and ministers, thereby establishing the source of the learning of the mind for all generations. From this arose their enlightened, harmonious, and expansive civilizing influence. Thereafter, ministers such as Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, together with the men of their time who performed distinguished service and discharged official duties, were all worthy and wise. What doubt could there be that their governance deserved to rank alongside that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun?

At that time, all those arrayed in official positions were Confucian scholars, so the designation “Confucian scholar” was not conspicuous. When the Way of Zhou declined day by day, learning fragmented into confusion, and the beneficial influence of Confucian scholars gradually disappeared from the world, Confucius had no choice but to proclaim his Way in Qi and Lu. On three occasions he expressed his concern with what it meant to be a Confucian scholar, and the designation then began to gain prominence. This can be understood by examining what he told Duke Ai. Yet he ultimately never obtained even one opportunity to put his teachings into practice.

After the Qin burial of scholars and the Han contempt for them, people instead used “Confucian scholar” as a term of mutual disparagement, and the name lost its standing and faded away. Fortunately, the law prohibiting possession of books was subsequently relaxed, and later there arose rulers such as Emperor Ming, who visited the imperial academy and bowed to its elders. Only then did people throughout the realm begin to admire Confucian scholars and seek learning. Yet from this time onward, what Confucian scholars actually were differed sharply from their ancient counterparts.

Thus, beginning with the Han, court historians came to recount their lives in separate biographical sections. The histories of the two Han dynasties contain “Biographies of Confucian Scholars”; those recorded there, such as Ding Kuan and Mou Rong, may be examined and understood. For the Tang, the title was changed to “Biographies of Confucian Learning”; those recorded there, such as Xu Wenyuan, may likewise be examined and understood. For the Song, the Han precedent was followed in compiling “Biographies of Confucian Scholars”; those from Nie Chongyi onward may also be examined and understood. Indeed, they were cultivated and numerous.

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
夫儒𥧌以盛而治則遞以衰所謂雜伯雜
夷委弱而不振者竟不能挽而躋之唐虞
三代之盛蓋嘗求其故矣或以訓詁辭章
為學而不能求之心或以高談性命為賢
而不能達之政故其學雖不同均之無補
于世也夫當漢之時六學殘缺諸子能窮
經於斷簡之中功非不多也但其學止于
訓詁不能融諸理性以臻自得如毛公治
詩而意多泥于章句京房說易而見多狃
===
于災異甚至守文滯固互相詭激誠有如
蔚宗所論者也以是槩之則其所謂訓詁
辭章猶不能無遺論矣况儒行乎欲其施
於天下國家難矣至于仲舒之下帷發憤
潛心大業猶為近之固乃別為傳述何也
彼之言曰古之學者博學六藝之文以此
為學則漢之諸儒可知矣當唐之時正學
晦蝕諸子能宗儒于陳隋之後志亦足尚
也但其學止于辨博不能反之於約以求

晦蝕諸子能宗儒于陳隋之後志亦足尚
也但其學止于辨博不能反之於約以求
punctuated:
夫儒𥧌以盛，而治則遞以衰，所謂雜伯雜夷、委弱而不振者，竟不能挽而躋之唐虞三代之盛。蓋嘗求其故矣：或以訓詁辭章為學，而不能求之心；或以高談性命為賢，而不能達之政。故其學雖不同，均之無補于世也。
夫當漢之時，六學殘缺，諸子能窮經於斷簡之中，功非不多也。但其學止于訓詁，不能融諸理性以臻自得。如毛公治詩，而意多泥于章句；京房說易，而見多狃于災異。甚至守文滯固，互相詭激，誠有如蔚宗所論者也。以是槩之，則其所謂訓詁辭章，猶不能無遺論矣，况儒行乎？欲其施於天下國家，難矣。至于仲舒之下帷發憤、潛心大業，猶為近之，固乃別為傳述，何也？彼之言曰：「古之學者，博學六藝之文。」以此為學，則漢之諸儒可知矣。
當唐之時，正學晦蝕，諸子能宗儒于陳隋之後，志亦足尚也。但其學止于辨博，不能反之於約以求
translation_en:
Now, as Confucian scholars gradually flourished, good government steadily declined. In what has been described as an admixture of hegemonic and barbarian practices, enfeebled and unable to recover, they ultimately could not reverse the decline and restore the flourishing government of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. I have sought the reasons for this. Some took textual glosses and literary composition as learning, but could not seek its foundations in the mind; others regarded lofty talk of human nature and destiny as worthiness, but could not bring it to bear on government. Thus, although their learning differed, they were alike in contributing nothing to the world.
During the Han, learning in the six classical disciplines was incomplete. These scholars were able to investigate the classics amid fragmentary texts, and their contributions were certainly considerable. Yet their learning stopped at textual glosses; they could not integrate it with principle and human nature to attain understanding for themselves. Master Mao, for example, studied the Book of Odes, but his interpretations were often mired in its divisions into chapters and sentences; Jing Fang expounded the Book of Changes, but his views were often confined to calamities and anomalies. They even clung rigidly to the written text and assailed one another with specious arguments, just as Weizong observed. Judged by this, even their supposed textual and literary scholarship could not escape criticism; how much less could their conduct as Confucians? To expect them to put their learning into practice in governing the realm and state was asking much. As for Dong Zhongshu, who lowered his study curtains, applied himself resolutely, and devoted his mind to the great undertaking, he came closer to the ideal. Yet Ban Gu gave him a separate biography—why? Ban Gu says: “Scholars of antiquity studied extensively the writings of the Six Arts.” If this was what counted as learning, the character of the Han Confucians becomes clear.
During the Tang, orthodox learning was obscured and diminished. That these scholars could take Confucian learning as their guiding authority after the Chen and Sui dynasties was an aspiration worthy of esteem. Yet their learning stopped at disputation and broad erudition; they could not return to its essentials in order to seek…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
實用如顏師古于十篇奇字討析非不熟
也而撰論必先貴勢孔穎達之五經正義
包貫非不詳也而嘉運猶多譏詆以至啖
助之言春秋則又失之鑿者也以是槩之
則其所謂訓詁辭章亦不能無遺論矣况
儒行乎欲其施于天下國家難矣至於韓
愈之文本六經皇皇仁義猶為近之史乃
别為傳述何也彼之言曰專誦習傳授者
次為儒學以此為儒則唐之諸儒可知矣
===
至宋承五季之衰去聖愈遠而學益離一時
儒者顧能以理學自振即其傳之所述經
術立教如胡瑗學行名節如邵伯温精詣
卓絕如蔡元定註脚六經如陸九淵以至
胡安國之進退合義真德秀之斯文自任
其視漢唐諸儒殆亦過矣然以周敦頤程
顥兄弟張載朱熹律之則妙契真際又非
數子所敢望史乃列為道學而不附儒林
則儒之所學者何學而所謂道學者獨非
alt_text:
實用如顏師古于十二篇音字討析非不熟
也而撰論必先貴於孔穎達之五經正義
包貫非不詳也而嘉運猶多譏詆以至啖
助之言春秋則又失之鑿者也以是槩之
則其所謂訓詁辭章亦不能無遺論矣况
儒行乎欲其施于天下國家難矣至於韓
愈之文本六經皇皇仁義猶爲近之史乃
別爲傳述何也彼之言曰專誦習傳授者
次爲儒學以此爲儒則唐之諸儒可知矣
===
至宋承五季之衰去聖愈遠而學益離一時
儒者顧能以理學自振即其傳之所述經
術立教如胡瑗學行名節如邵伯温精詣
卓絶如蔡元定註脚六經如陸九淵以至
胡安國之進退合義真德秀之斯文自任
其視漢唐諸儒殆亦過矣然以周敦頤程
顥兄弟張載朱熹律之則妙契真際又非
數子所敢望史乃列爲道學而不附儒林
則儒之所學者何事而所謂道學者獨非
punctuated:
實用。如顏師古于十篇奇字，討析非不熟也，而撰論必先貴勢；孔穎達之《五經正義》，包貫非不詳也，而嘉運猶多譏詆；以至啖助之言《春秋》，則又失之鑿者也。以是槩之，則其所謂訓詁辭章，亦不能無遺論矣，况儒行乎？欲其施于天下國家，難矣。至於韓愈之文本六經，皇皇仁義，猶為近之，史乃别為傳述，何也？彼之言曰：「專誦習傳授者，次為儒學。」以此為儒，則唐之諸儒可知矣。

至宋，承五季之衰，去聖愈遠，而學益離。一時儒者，顧能以理學自振。即其傳之所述，經術立教如胡瑗，學行名節如邵伯温，精詣卓絕如蔡元定，註脚六經如陸九淵，以至胡安國之進退合義、真德秀之斯文自任，其視漢唐諸儒，殆亦過矣。然以周敦頤、程顥兄弟、張載、朱熹律之，則妙契真際，又非數子所敢望。史乃列為道學，而不附儒林，則儒之所學者何學，而所謂道學者獨非
translation_en:
…practical application. Yan Shigu, for example, was certainly well versed in examining and analyzing the unusual characters of the “ten chapters” [?], yet in composing his discussions he invariably gave precedence to the powerful and eminent. Kong Yingda’s Correct Meaning of the Five Classics was certainly comprehensive and detailed, yet Jiayun still subjected it to much criticism. As for Dan Zhu’s treatment of the Spring and Autumn Annals, it erred in forcing interpretations. Judged by these examples, even their so-called textual exegesis and literary composition cannot escape criticism; how much more questionable was their conduct as Confucians! It would have been difficult to apply their learning to governing the realm and the state. Han Yu’s writings, however, were rooted in the Six Classics and shone with benevolence and righteousness, thus coming somewhat closer to the ideal. Why, then, did the history give him a separate biography? It says: “Those who devoted themselves exclusively to recitation, study, and transmission were arranged under ‘Confucian Learning.’” If this is what counted as Confucianism, we can understand what the Confucians of the Tang were like.

By the Song, which inherited the decline of the Five Dynasties, the sages were ever more remote, and learning had departed still further from them. Yet the Confucians of that age were able to revive themselves through the learning of principle. Consider what their biographies record: Hu Yuan established teaching through mastery of the Classics; Shao Bowen was distinguished for learning, conduct, reputation, and integrity; Cai Yuanding attained exceptional depth and precision; Lu Jiuyuan supplied explanatory glosses to the Six Classics. There were also Hu Anguo, whose decisions to serve or withdraw accorded with righteousness, and Zhen Dexiu, who took responsibility for this cultural tradition upon himself. Compared with the Confucians of the Han and Tang, they surely surpassed them. Yet measured against Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao and his brother, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, these scholars could not dare hope to equal their subtle accord with ultimate truth. The history nevertheless classified the latter under ‘Learning of the Way’ rather than including them in ‘The Forest of Confucians.’ What learning, then, did Confucians pursue, and were those called practitioners of the Learning of the Way alone not…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
儒哉宋儒之盛如此然竟無補於其時或
迂而未適于用或用而未究其施此又誰
執其咎邪大抵學也者根於一心而妙於
萬化者也歛之無聲無臭而非淪於虛擴
之有猷有為而非滯於迹體之身而無怍
於鬼神之謂德措之政而有裨於生民之
謂功發揮於詞體物撰德可傳於後世之
謂言故曰太上立德其次立功其次立言
然三者德其本也有其德矣得志而行之
===
則立功如皐陶伊傅周召是也不得志而
藏之則立言如孔孟是也又其次也則宋
之周程張朱真可以遠紹孔孟之傳而漢
之仲舒唐之韓愈亦不足以語此何也舒
則學而未純愈則以文為學其于道皆未
有得也其能以達之政哉故嘗謂熈寧乾
道之間委數子而授之政必可以致于理
而仲舒即不淹於江都韓愈即不擯於朝
陽終不能致建元元和之世於唐虞三代

萬化者也歛之無聲無臭而非淪於虛擴
之有猷有為而非滯於迹體之身而無怍
於鬼神之謂德措之政而有裨於生民之
謂功發揮於詞體物撰德可傳於後世之
謂言故曰太上立德其次立功其次立言
然三者德其本也有其德矣得志而行之
===
則立功如皐陶伊傅周召是也不得志而
藏之則立言如孔孟是也又其次也則宋
之周程張朱真可以遠紹孔孟之傳而漢
之仲舒唐之韓愈亦不足以語此何也舒
則學而未純愈則以文為學其于道皆未
有得也其能以達之政哉故嘗謂熙寧乾
道之間要數子而授之政必可以致于理
而仲舒即不淹於江都韓愈即不擯於朝
陽終不能致建元元和之世於唐虞三代
punctuated: 儒哉？宋儒之盛如此，然竟無補於其時，或迂而未適于用，或用而未究其施，此又誰執其咎邪？大抵學也者，根於一心而妙於萬化者也。歛之無聲無臭，而非淪於虛；擴之有猷有為，而非滯於迹。體之身而無怍於鬼神之謂德，措之政而有裨於生民之謂功，發揮於詞、體物撰德、可傳於後世之謂言。故曰：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」然三者，德其本也。有其德矣，得志而行之，則立功，如皐陶、伊、傅、周、召是也；不得志而藏之，則立言，如孔、孟是也。又其次也，則宋之周、程、張、朱，真可以遠紹孔、孟之傳，而漢之仲舒、唐之韓愈亦不足以語此。何也？舒則學而未純，愈則以文為學，其于道皆未有得也，其能以達之政哉？故嘗謂熈寧、乾道之間，委數子而授之政，必可以致于理；而仲舒即不淹於江都，韓愈即不擯於朝陽，終不能致建元、元和之世於唐虞三代
translation_en:
…Confucian scholars? Such was the flourishing of Confucian scholarship under the Song, yet in the end it brought no benefit to its own age. Some scholars were too impractical to be suited to employment; others were employed but could not fully carry out their aims. Who, then, should bear the blame for this?

Learning, in its broadest sense, is rooted in the single mind and works wondrously through the myriad transformations. Gathered inward, it is without sound or scent, yet does not lapse into emptiness; extended outward, it produces plans and deeds, yet does not become mired in outward traces. To embody it in oneself and feel no shame before ghosts and spirits is what is called virtue. To apply it in government and benefit the people is what is called achievement. To express it in words, give form to things and articulate virtue, so that it may be transmitted to later generations, is what is called enduring speech. Thus it is said: “Highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievement; next is establishing enduring speech.” Of these three, however, virtue is the foundation. Possessing this virtue, if one attains one's aspirations and puts it into practice, one establishes achievement: Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao are examples. If one does not attain one's aspirations and keeps it within, one establishes enduring speech: Kongzi and Mengzi are examples.

Next after them, Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi of the Song could truly carry forward the tradition of Kongzi and Mengzi across the intervening ages. Yet even Dong Zhongshu of the Han and Han Yu of the Tang do not qualify to be spoken of in these terms. Why? Zhongshu's learning was not pure, while Han Yu took literary composition to be learning. Neither had attained an understanding of the Way. How could they bring it to bear upon government?

Thus I have maintained that, in the period between the Xining and Qiandao reign eras, had those several masters been entrusted with governmental authority, they would surely have brought about good order. But even if Zhongshu had not languished in Jiangdu, and Han Yu had not been banished to Chaoyang [?], they could never have brought the ages of Jianyuan and Yuanhe up to the level of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
者凡以此耳後之言儒者乃執不學者之
效以槩儒之無補於治則是因亢溢而廢
農因苦窳而廢工也其可廢乎哉無農而
天下病於食矣無工而天下病於用矣無
儒臣而天下病於治矣故農而不穫者有
之未有舍農而求食者也工而不精者有
之未有舍工而求器者也儒而無益於治
者有之未有舍儒而求治者也然則天下
誠不可一日無儒而儒之所以自待者亦
===
豈可甚自菲薄也哉孔子有之曰女為君
子儒無為小人儒易曰正其本萬事理差
之毫釐謬以千里幾微之際世之治忽係
焉何可以無慎乎哉愚不敏敢不因名究
實以求無負於
崇儒重道之世
第五問
陳斗南
同考試官員外郎朱 批 安據

豈可甚自菲薄也哉孔子有之曰女為君

之毫釐謬以千里幾微之際世之治忽係
焉何可以無愼乎哉愚不敏敢不因名究
實以求無負於
崇儒重道之世
第五問
陳斗南
同考試官員外郎李 批 安據
punctuated:
者，凡以此耳。後之言儒者，乃執不學者之效，以槩儒之無補於治，則是因亢溢而廢農，因苦窳而廢工也。其可廢乎哉？無農而天下病於食矣，無工而天下病於用矣，無儒臣而天下病於治矣。故農而不穫者有之，未有舍農而求食者也；工而不精者有之，未有舍工而求器者也；儒而無益於治者有之，未有舍儒而求治者也。然則天下誠不可一日無儒，而儒之所以自待者，亦豈可甚自菲薄也哉？孔子有之，曰：「女為君子儒，無為小人儒。」《易》曰：「正其本，萬事理；差之毫釐，謬以千里。」幾微之際，世之治忽係焉，何可以無慎乎哉？愚不敏，敢不因名究實，以求無負於崇儒重道之世？

第五問
陳斗南
同考試官員外郎朱批：安據
translation_en:
…all for these reasons alone. Yet later commentators on Confucian scholars seize upon the results achieved by men without learning to conclude sweepingly that Confucian scholars contribute nothing to good government. This is like abandoning agriculture because of droughts and floods, or abandoning craftsmanship because of shoddy workmanship. Can they possibly be abandoned? Without farmers, all under Heaven would suffer for want of food; without craftsmen, all under Heaven would suffer for want of useful goods; without Confucian ministers, all under Heaven would suffer for want of good government. Thus, there are farmers who reap no harvest, but no one abandons farming and still seeks food. There are craftsmen whose work lacks refinement, but no one abandons craftsmanship and still seeks utensils. There are Confucian scholars who bring no benefit to government, but no one abandons Confucian learning and still seeks good government. If, then, the world truly cannot do without Confucian scholars for even a single day, how can those scholars hold themselves in such low esteem?

Confucius said: “Be a Confucian scholar of the gentlemanly kind, not a Confucian scholar of the petty kind.” The Book of Changes says: “Set the root right, and all affairs will be ordered; deviate by a hair’s breadth, and the error will extend a thousand li.” Upon the subtlest distinctions depend order and disorder in the world. How could one fail to exercise care? Foolish and slow of understanding as I am, dare I fail to examine the substance behind the name, seeking to prove worthy of an age that honors Confucian learning and esteems the Way?

Fifth Policy Question
Chen Dounan
Associate Examiner Zhu, Vice Director, comments: “Securely grounded [?]…”

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
國家大計此策考據詳明籌畫精確具見卓識所謂書生
抱經濟之畧者子非其人邪
同考試官郎中盧批邊計士子類能言之
獨此篇深探往事區畫時宜盖嘗懷治世之隱
憂究心而有得者豈特文詞之工而已哉
同考試官編修吳批論邊計必歸諸勝筭
洋洋皆董賈言發之可易得哉可易得哉
同考試官修撰李批邊務書生罕究心者
子能歷歷言之且皆可措之行事胸中甲兵
殆不可測已
===
同考試官修撰王批今談說世故人人能
矣至効實則難焉子之言兵固也尚思取
以効實者哉
考試官學士歐陽批勝虜以多算故將兵將
將貴識子之六計引而未發吾以是占子之識
矣進子以待熟數之非獨以文之古也
考試官大學士張批兵法談古事易說今事
難時不同也子既明習當世之務而能以古論

矣至効實則難焉子之言兵固也尚思取
以効實者哉

矣進子以待熟數之非獨以文之古也
考試官大學士張　批　兵法談古事易說今事
難時不同也子既明習當世之務而能以古論
punctuated:
國家大計，此策考據詳明，籌畫精確，具見卓識。所謂書生抱經濟之畧者，子非其人邪？

同考試官郎中盧批：邊計，士子類能言之，獨此篇深探往事，區畫時宜，盖嘗懷治世之隱憂，究心而有得者，豈特文詞之工而已哉？

同考試官編修吳批：論邊計，必歸諸勝筭。洋洋皆董賈言，發之可易得哉？可易得哉？

同考試官修撰李批：邊務，書生罕究心者。子能歷歷言之，且皆可措之行事，胸中甲兵，殆不可測已。

同考試官修撰王批：今談說世故，人人能矣；至効實，則難焉。子之言兵固也，尚思取以効實者哉！

考試官學士歐陽批：勝虜以多算，故將兵、將將貴識。子之六計，引而未發，吾以是占子之識矣。進子以待熟數之，非獨以文之古也。

考試官大學士張批：兵法，談古事易，說今事難，時不同也。子既明習當世之務，而能以古論
translation_en:
…the great plans of the state. This policy essay is detailed and clear in its examination of evidence, and precise in its planning; it displays outstanding discernment throughout. Are you not what is called a scholar possessed of strategies for governing the realm?

Associate Examiner Lu, Director, comments: Candidates generally can discuss frontier strategy, but this essay alone probes deeply into past events and devises measures appropriate to present circumstances. Its author must have harbored concern over the hidden troubles of an age of good government, and reached insights through sustained reflection. How could this be merely skill in literary expression?

Associate Examiner Wu, Compiler, comments: Discussion of frontier strategy must ultimately rest on calculations that secure victory. This expansive exposition consists entirely of words worthy of Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi. Could such an exposition be easily attained? Could it be easily attained?

Associate Examiner Li, Senior Compiler, comments: Frontier affairs are a subject to which scholars seldom devote serious thought. You can explain them point by point, and all your proposals can be put into practice. The military resources within your breast are surely unfathomable.

Associate Examiner Wang, Senior Compiler, comments: Nowadays everyone can discuss worldly affairs; achieving practical results is difficult. Your discussion of military matters is sound. May you also consider how to put it into practice and obtain results!

Examiner Ouyang, Academician, comments: Victory over the enemy comes through ample calculation; thus, whether commanding soldiers or commanding generals, discernment is prized. Your six strategies draw the bow without yet releasing the arrow, and from this I judge your discernment. I advance you in anticipation of your weighing these matters thoroughly, not solely because your prose has the quality of antiquity.

Examiner Zhang, Grand Secretary, comments: In military strategy, discussing ancient affairs is easy, but discussing present affairs is difficult, because the times differ. You already understand the affairs of the present age clearly and thoroughly, and can draw upon ancient discussions…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
發之各有攸當豈亦胸中有甲兵者乎
執事以制夷安邊之畧下詢承學愚也何
從與知之哉雖然竊亦有聞焉而思以効
之也愚聞正德中虜酋駐牧威寧海子威
寧在宣大二鎮間時王恭襄在本兵晝聞
乃即選大將一人參將二人督京營兵練
習之又徵遼東兵赴薊州備之又檄宣大
整兵備之既半歲虜不來申令營兵在練
者無得怠諸鎮兵亦不解忽而虜果入白
===
羊口南嚮而趨居庸晝連至告急乃即遣
所選將所練士出擊之遼東兵自左臂至
宣大兵隨肩背至諸軍既合虜狼顧駭慄
一日輒移去是歲也虜春駐威寧秋乃始
入者伺我懈而冀得縱也借使我兵以久
待不至弛焉彼計中矣盖虜凡大入必招
集諸部落以利啗之不得利不足示信自
虜駐威寧即識其計而備之若恭襄者真
謀臣也又聞正德中朶顏酋長花當之子

者無得怠諸鎮兵亦不解弛而虜果入白

羊口南嚮而趨邊庸書邊至告急乃即遣
所選將所練士出擊之遼東兵自左臂至
宣大兵隨肩背至諸軍既合虜狼顧駭慄
一日輒移去是歲也虜春駐威寧秋乃始
入者伺我懈而冀得縱也借使我兵以久
待不至弛馬彼計中矣蓋虜凡大入必招
集諸部落以利啗之不得利不足示信自
厲駐威寧即識其計而備之若恭襄者真
謀臣也又聞正德中朶顏酋長花當之子
punctuated:
發之，各有攸當，豈亦胸中有甲兵者乎？

執事以制夷安邊之畧下詢承學，愚也何從與知之哉？雖然，竊亦有聞焉，而思以効之也。愚聞正德中，虜酋駐牧威寧海子。威寧在宣大二鎮間。時王恭襄在本兵，晝聞，乃即選大將一人、參將二人，督京營兵練習之；又徵遼東兵赴薊州備之；又檄宣大整兵備之。既半歲，虜不來，申令營兵在練者無得怠，諸鎮兵亦不解。忽而虜果入白羊口，南嚮而趨居庸，晝連至告急，乃即遣所選將、所練士出擊之。遼東兵自左臂至，宣大兵隨肩背至。諸軍既合，虜狼顧駭慄，一日輒移去。是歲也，虜春駐威寧，秋乃始入者，伺我懈而冀得縱也。借使我兵以久待不至弛焉，彼計中矣。盖虜凡大入，必招集諸部落，以利啗之，不得利不足示信。自虜駐威寧，即識其計而備之，若恭襄者，真謀臣也。又聞正德中，朶顏酋長花當之子
translation_en:
…expound them, each fitting its purpose. Might you too be one who carries armies within his breast?

You have graciously asked us students about strategies for controlling the foreign peoples and securing the frontier. How could someone as ignorant as I have any knowledge of these matters? Nevertheless, I have privately heard something of them and have considered how to put it to practical use. I have heard that during the Zhengde reign, an enemy chieftain encamped with his herds at Weining Haizi. Weining lies between the two garrisons of Xuanfu and Datong. At that time Wang Gongxiang was Minister of War. Upon hearing the news [?], he immediately selected one senior commander and two assistant regional commanders to supervise the training of troops from the capital camps. He also summoned troops from Liaodong to Jizhou to prepare against the enemy and sent orders to Xuanfu and Datong to ready their troops for defense. After half a year had passed without the enemy coming, he reiterated that the camp troops undergoing training must not slacken; the troops in the various garrisons likewise maintained their readiness. Suddenly the enemy did indeed enter through Baiyangkou, heading south toward Juyong. Urgent reports arrived in succession [?], and he immediately dispatched the commanders he had selected and the soldiers he had trained to attack them. The Liaodong troops arrived on their left flank, while the Xuanfu and Datong troops came up behind their shoulders and rear. Once the armies had joined forces, the enemy looked fearfully about like wolves, trembling in alarm, and withdrew within a day.

That year, the enemy encamped at Weining in spring but did not invade until autumn because they were waiting for us to grow lax, hoping then to have free rein. Had our troops relaxed because they had waited so long without the enemy arriving, the enemy's plan would have succeeded. Whenever the enemy undertakes a major invasion, they must gather the various tribes, enticing them with the prospect of gain; without securing that gain, they cannot demonstrate their trustworthiness. To recognize their plan and prepare against it from the moment they encamped at Weining—as Gongxiang did—was truly the work of a strategic minister. I have also heard that during the Zhengde reign, the son of Huadang, chieftain of Duoyan…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
寇馬蘭谷也參將陳乾禦之花當子射乾
乾死恭襄乃請遣使責問花當即如花當
不知則執其子来歸償罪花當不坐不服
則起大兵伐之以遼東兵攻其左以宣大
兵攻其右破滅必矣花當懼服如今夫花
當夷種也輕生善闘豈憚我兵哉貪漢財
物如啖甘蔗舍而弗忍唾之也恭襄習之
故花當寧棄其子竟不絕漢好即如忍而
不問將無忌矣今若此則是爵賞之恩予
===
其降伏誅罰之典咎其犯順威惠並著以
革其奸而誘其衷若恭襄者真謀臣也又
聞成化末海西夷之犯遼東也驅掠甚盛
我軍半創死本兵馬端肅議曰夫海西夷
降虜也今来犯是不降也勦之宜否則長
驁而狎中國之恩守臣陳越曰勦必啓釁
撫之宜
詔從本兵議乃命將出師直臨賊境誅戮俘馘
以千百數赫赫燁燁威振殊俗矣夫女直

乾死恭襄乃請遣使責問花當即如花當
不知則執其子來歸償罪花當不坐不服

===

華其奸而誘其衆若恭襄者真謀臣也又
聞成化末海西夷之犯遼東也驅掠甚盛
我軍半創死本兵馬端肅議曰夫海西夷
降屬也今來犯是不降也勦之宜一否則長
驁而狎中國之恩守臣陳越日勦必啓釁
撫之宜
詔從本兵議乃命將出師直臨賊境誅戮俘馘
以千百數赫赫煒煒威振殊俗矣夫文直
punctuated:

…raided Malan Valley. Regional Commander Chen Qian resisted him, but Huadang’s son shot Chen Qian, who died. Gongxiang then requested that an envoy be sent to call Huadang to account: if Huadang had indeed been unaware, he should seize his son and deliver him to atone for the crime, and Huadang himself would not be held liable. If he refused to submit, a great army should be raised against him, with troops from Liaodong attacking his left and troops from Xuanfu and Datong attacking his right. His destruction would then be certain. Huadang was frightened and submitted. Now Huadang was of barbarian stock, reckless of life and skilled in fighting: could he really have feared our troops? He coveted Chinese wealth and goods as one relishes sugarcane, unable to bear spitting it out and giving it up. Gongxiang understood this well. Thus Huadang preferred to abandon his son and ultimately did not sever friendly relations with China. Had we tolerated the act without calling him to account, he would have known no restraint. Acting thus meant bestowing the favor of ranks and rewards upon his submission, while applying the statutes of execution and punishment to his offense against imperial authority. Might and beneficence were displayed together to reform his treachery and draw forth his sincerity. A man such as Gongxiang was truly a discerning counselor.
I have also heard that, at the end of the Chenghua reign, when the Haixi barbarians invaded Liaodong, they carried off people and plunder on a vast scale, and half our troops were wounded or killed. The Minister of War, Ma Duansu, proposed: “The Haixi barbarians are foes who have submitted. By coming to invade now, they show that they no longer submit. It is fitting to suppress them. Otherwise, we shall foster their arrogance and cause them to treat the kindness of the Central Kingdom with contempt.” The official charged with defending the region, Chen Yue, said: “Suppression will certainly provoke hostilities. It is fitting to pacify them.” An imperial edict adopted the Minister of War’s proposal. A commander was therefore ordered to lead an expedition directly into the enemy’s territory. Those killed or captured, and the ears taken from the slain, numbered in the hundreds and thousands. Brilliant and resplendent, imperial might shook peoples of alien customs. Now, the Jurchens…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
嘗起海西據中土非細物也犯而顧撫之
是彼制我也今勦之是我制彼也其時余
肅敏議之曰寧成功于門庭之間勿遠致
于敵人之境斯馭夷之恒調非適時之大
權也若端肅者真謀臣也夫謀臣之在事
也未事而畫之則為之計利害籌多少視
遠視近校彼校我若大賈行貨度三五之
數而等貴賤之利也其畫定而舉也不可
諧奪不可禍怵信性迅邁飄飄乎若鷙鳥
===
之摶也若峽水下舟而放之疾也故始無
輕發卒鮮隳事後至者弗可弗稽也夫大
匠以目中然未有離繩墨巧者也上醫以
意中然未有舍方書神者也兵亦若是而
已頃歲以来朶顏諸部恒出兵以撓薊疆
不宜置之不問且
國家所以懷夷者甚厚而久授爵降印世世
弗替乃復和親北虜市外交而恐喝疆埸
之臣以要賞益貨否則来侵弗可狃也可

于敵人之境斯馭夷之恒調非適時之大

輕發卒鮮頹落𡚒後至者弗可弗籍也夫大

意中然未有舍規神者也兵亦若是而
已頃歲以來朶顏諸部恒出兵以撓薊疆
不宜置之不問且
國家所以懷夷者甚厚而久授爵陞印世世

punctuated: 嘗起海西，據中土，非細物也。犯而顧撫之，是彼制我也；今勦之，是我制彼也。其時余肅敏議之曰：「寧成功于門庭之間，勿遠致于敵人之境。」斯馭夷之恒調，非適時之大權也。若端肅者，真謀臣也。夫謀臣之在事也，未事而畫之，則為之計利害，籌多少，視遠視近，校彼校我，若大賈行貨，度三五之數而等貴賤之利也。其畫定而舉也，不可諧奪，不可禍怵，信性迅邁，飄飄乎若鷙鳥之摶也，若峽水下舟而放之疾也。故始無輕發，卒鮮隳事，後至者弗可弗稽也。夫大匠以目中，然未有離繩墨巧者也；上醫以意中，然未有舍方書神者也。兵亦若是而已。頃歲以来，朶顏諸部恒出兵以撓薊疆，不宜置之不問。且國家所以懷夷者甚厚而久，授爵降印，世世弗替。乃復和親北虜，市外交，而恐喝疆埸之臣，以要賞益貨，否則来侵，弗可狃也。可
translation_en:
…once arose in Haixi and occupied the Central Lands; they are no insignificant force. If, after they invade, we nevertheless seek to conciliate them, they control us. If we now suppress them, we control them. At that time Yu Sumin argued: “Better to achieve success within our own gates than to pursue it far away in the enemy’s territory.” This is the ordinary approach to managing the foreign peoples, not the exceptional exercise of discretion suited to the circumstances. A man such as Duansu is truly a minister of strategic counsel.

When such a minister handles affairs, he plans before acting: he calculates advantages and disadvantages, reckons quantities, considers distant and immediate concerns, and compares the enemy’s position with our own. He is like a great merchant trading goods, reckoning figures of three and five [?] and assessing the profits from high and low prices. Once his plan is settled and put into action, he cannot be diverted by persuasion [?] or frightened by disaster. Trusting his own disposition, he advances swiftly, soaring like a bird of prey striking, or racing like a boat launched downstream through a gorge. Thus he does not act rashly at the outset and seldom brings affairs to ruin in the end. Those who come after him must examine these precedents. A master carpenter judges accurately by eye, yet none has achieved skill apart from the marking line; a superior physician judges accurately by intuition, yet none has achieved marvelous results while abandoning medical formularies. Warfare is simply the same.

In recent years, the various Duoyan tribes have repeatedly sent troops to harass the Ji frontier. This should not be left unaddressed. Moreover, the state has long treated these foreign peoples with great generosity to win their allegiance, granting noble titles and bestowing seals, without interruption from generation to generation. Yet they have also established friendly ties with the northern foes and sought outside alliances, threatening frontier officials to demand rewards and additional goods, and invading if these are withheld. They must not be allowed to grow accustomed to this. It would be possible to…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
及其来
朝諭之禍福戒勿負恩絶好其撓邊甚者按
依前事固求其人罪之卒之蒙罪者少被
賞者多少不勝多則威不勝徳不傷國重
不起禍階則柔顔可常服也海西諸夷屋
居田作與中國同射獵侵掠與北虜同盖
兼二俗有之兼二俗則易制也夫屋居田
作則內顧重內顧重則搗巢之令得懾其
奸且彼內附久則信義可責於其来侵時
===
出銳師以逆境上名曰搗巢按且勿進令
来歸義兵乃解此既歸義則要取盟誓文
書以持後事夷即難信結我将兵之有詞
也如此則勦存撫情撫寓勦威海西夷可
常服也至若北虜制之固有舊算而効卒
罕睹何者庸将先失之懦将後失之也何
謂先失之虜将大入其兵非一日能集也
又其性儇黠結營在此所向在彼倏東倏
□疾於烏舉此彼醜恒態也覘者至苟得

作則内顧重内顧重則搗巢之令得攝其
奸且彼内附久則信義可責於其来侵時
===
出鋭師以逆境上名曰搗巢按且勿進令
来歸義兵乃解比既歸義則要取盟誓文
書以持後事夷即難信結我将兵之有詞
也如此則勦存撫情撫寓勦威海西夷可
常服也至若北虜制之固有舊算而効卒
罕睹何者庸将先失之懦将後失之也何
謂先失之虜将大入其兵非一日能集也
又其性儇黠結營在此所向在彼條東條
□□於鳥舉此彼醜恒態也覘者至苟得
punctuated:
及其来朝，諭之禍福，戒勿負恩絶好。其撓邊甚者，按依前事，固求其人罪之。卒之蒙罪者少，被賞者多，少不勝多，則威不勝徳。不傷國重，不起禍階，則柔顔可常服也。
海西諸夷，屋居田作與中國同，射獵侵掠與北虜同，盖兼二俗有之。兼二俗，則易制也。夫屋居田作，則內顧重；內顧重，則搗巢之令得懾其奸。且彼內附久，則信義可責。於其来侵時，出銳師以逆境上，名曰搗巢，按且勿進，令来歸義，兵乃解。此既歸義，則要取盟誓文書，以持後事。夷即難信，結我将兵之有詞也。如此，則勦存撫情，撫寓勦威，海西夷可常服也。
至若北虜，制之固有舊算，而効卒罕睹。何者？庸将先失之，懦将後失之也。何謂先失之？虜将大入，其兵非一日能集也。又其性儇黠，結營在此，所向在彼，倏東倏□，疾於烏舉，此彼醜恒態也。覘者至，苟得
translation_en:
…when they come to court, explain to them the calamities and blessings that await them, and warn them against betraying imperial favor and severing friendly relations. For those who have most seriously disturbed the frontier, follow earlier precedents, insist upon obtaining the offenders themselves [?], and punish them. In the end, those punished will be few and those rewarded many. Since the few do not outweigh the many, severity will not outweigh beneficence. Without impairing the state's dignity or opening the way to disaster, the Rouyan [?] can thus be kept continually submissive.
The various peoples of Haixi live in houses and cultivate fields like those of China, but hunt with bows and engage in raids and plunder like the northern barbarians. They thus combine both ways of life. Combining both makes them easy to control. Living in houses and cultivating fields gives them weighty concerns at home; with such concerns, an order to strike their home settlements can deter their wrongdoing. Moreover, they have long submitted to our authority, so fidelity and righteousness may be demanded of them. When they invade, send picked troops to meet them at the frontier, declaring an intention to strike their home settlements, but hold the troops back from advancing. Order them to come and submit to righteousness; only then should the troops stand down. Once they have submitted, require written pledges and oaths to provide grounds for handling subsequent affairs. Even if these peoples are difficult to trust, this will establish a justification for our deployment of troops [?]. In this way, punitive operations will retain an intent to pacify, while pacification will embody the deterrent force of punitive operations. The peoples of Haixi can thus be kept continually submissive.
As for the northern barbarians, established plans for controlling them certainly exist, yet results are seldom seen. Why? Mediocre generals fail at the outset, and cowardly generals fail afterward. What is meant by failing at the outset? When the barbarians intend a major invasion, their forces cannot be assembled in a single day. Moreover, they are quick and cunning by nature: they encamp here but aim to strike there, suddenly moving east and suddenly □, swifter than a crow taking flight. Such is the habitual conduct of those villains. When scouts arrive, if they obtain…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
虜情能即發符徴兵分地據守又於要害
之口必從之路多張旗幟盛振金鼓示形
以必不可犯示間以必不可乗虜衆望見
憚不敢逼守之無何且移去矣而將不早
圖遂令穿塞而入肆螫我土故曰先失之
也此智不能照謀不能先故曰庸也何謂
後失之虜既入塞或合十萬之衆結為一
營而我軍數萬分為數處勢不相當安可
進取惟得利歸也則所得有多寡彼醜有
===
喜怒及既出塞輙各分散不相顧藉苟候
之歸路谿谷之間阸塞之處伏兵邀擊奪
獲畜産即以其半與之宣大之人習勇好
利將奮九死應矣而將不此圖遂令十来
十歸窮来富歸虜無遺矢缺戕之勞而安
取漢財如索諸寄故曰後失之也此其保
爵愛身懾禍求全故曰懦也且彼既僨事
矣而始罪之罪之當也無救于僨也故選
將恒談而制虜之術要不出此其若選將

之歸路谿谷之間阨塞之處伏兵邀擊奪

矣而始罪之罪之當也無救于僨也故選
將恒談而制虜之術要不出此其若選將
punctuated: 虜情，能即發符徴兵，分地據守，又於要害之口、必從之路，多張旗幟，盛振金鼓，示形以必不可犯，示間以必不可乗，虜衆望見，憚不敢逼，守之無何，且移去矣。而將不早圖，遂令穿塞而入，肆螫我土，故曰先失之也。此智不能照，謀不能先，故曰庸也。何謂後失之？虜既入塞，或合十萬之衆，結為一營，而我軍數萬，分為數處，勢不相當，安可進取？惟得利歸也，則所得有多寡，彼醜有喜怒；及既出塞，輙各分散，不相顧藉。苟候之歸路，谿谷之間、阸塞之處，伏兵邀擊，奪獲畜産，即以其半與之，宣大之人習勇好利，將奮九死應矣。而將不此圖，遂令十来十歸，窮来富歸，虜無遺矢缺戕之勞，而安取漢財，如索諸寄，故曰後失之也。此其保爵愛身，懾禍求全，故曰懦也。且彼既僨事矣，而始罪之，罪之當也，無救于僨也。故選將恒談，而制虜之術要不出此。其若選將
translation_en:
…the enemy’s situation, and could immediately issue warrants to summon troops and assign them positions to hold, while also displaying numerous banners and loudly sounding gongs and drums at strategic passes and along routes the enemy must take—showing dispositions that could not be attacked and gaps that could not be exploited—then the enemy host, seeing these from afar, would be intimidated and dare not approach. After we had held our positions for only a short time, they would move away. Yet the commander fails to plan early, thus allowing them to penetrate the frontier defenses and wreak harm upon our land. This is what is meant by failing beforehand. His intelligence cannot discern what is coming, and his planning cannot anticipate it; hence he is called mediocre.

What is meant by failing afterward? Once the enemy has entered the frontier, they may unite a host of a hundred thousand into one encampment, while our several tens of thousands of soldiers are divided among several positions. With forces so unequal, how could we advance against them? But when they return with their gains, some have obtained more and others less, and among those villains some are pleased and others angry. Once beyond the frontier, they each disperse, taking no care for one another. If we waited along their homeward route, setting ambushes in ravines and at constricted passes to intercept them, seized their livestock, and immediately gave half to our soldiers, the men of Xuanfu and Datong, accustomed to acts of valor and eager for profit, would respond with vigor, braving death a hundred times over. Yet the commander fails to plan for this, thus allowing all who come to return, arriving poor and departing rich. Without even the trouble of expending arrows or damaging weapons [?], the enemy takes Han wealth at ease, as though reclaiming property left in safekeeping. This is what is meant by failing afterward. The commander protects his rank and cherishes his own person, fears disaster and seeks to keep himself unscathed; hence he is called cowardly.

Moreover, only after such a man has already ruined affairs do we begin to punish him. Punishing him is appropriate, but it cannot remedy the ruin. Thus, although selecting commanders is a commonplace topic, the essential method of controlling the enemy goes no further than this. As for selecting commanders…

title: 嘉靖二十九年會試錄
text:
則莫如守臣自薦所知本兵因視所宜任
之守臣得良將則外有與本兵得良將則
内有恃殆無憂制虜之術矣雖然本兵守
臣此兩臣者尤要也尤要則尤宜擇也是
故
天子内擇本兵非有識者弗與也外擇守臣非
有識者弗與也兩臣者起而應擇内者量
力未能勝弗敢舉也外者量勢未能運弗
敢任也上擇固精下量又審則才者處權
===
才者處權而疆圉之不固者無有也本有
他長授以樞筦則用非其能用非其能而
責疆圉之必固安有也故兩臣先識無識
者弗可與也彼王恭襄馬端肅者並以識
勝不識其識則不用其謀故國有識者又
貴識識者何也百年之計不可以目前効
而見在眉睫者謂迂也獨睹之計不可令
衆庶見而不得其指者謂詭也持重之計
似怯趨時之計似輕勝計佯敗取計佯與

之守臣得良將則外有與本兵得良將則

臣此兩臣者尤要也尤要則尤宜擇也是
故
天子內擇本兵非有識者弗與也外擇守臣非
有識者弗與也兩臣者起而應擇內者量
力未能勝弗敢舉也外者量勢未能運弗
敢任也上擇固精下量又審則才者處權
才者處權而疆圉之不固者無有也本有
他長授以樞管則用非其能用非其能而
責疆圉之必固安有也故兩臣先識無識
者弗可與也彼王恭襄馬端肅者並以識
勝不識其識則不用其謀故國有識者又
貴識識者何也百年之計不可以目前効
而見在眉睫者謂迂也獨睹之計不可令
衆庶見而不得其指者謂詭也持重之計
似怯趨時之計似輕勝計佯敗敗計佯與
punctuated: 則莫如守臣自薦所知，本兵因視所宜任之。守臣得良將，則外有與；本兵得良將，則内有恃，殆無憂制虜之術矣。雖然，本兵、守臣，此兩臣者尤要也。尤要則尤宜擇也。是故天子内擇本兵，非有識者弗與也；外擇守臣，非有識者弗與也。兩臣者起而應擇，内者量力，未能勝弗敢舉也；外者量勢，未能運弗敢任也。上擇固精，下量又審，則才者處權。才者處權，而疆圉之不固者，無有也。本有他長，授以樞筦，則用非其能；用非其能，而責疆圉之必固，安有也？故兩臣先識，無識者弗可與也。彼王恭襄、馬端肅者，並以識勝。不識其識，則不用其謀。故國有識者，又貴識識者。何也？百年之計，不可以目前効，而見在眉睫者謂迂也；獨睹之計，不可令衆庶見，而不得其指者謂詭也；持重之計似怯，趨時之計似輕，勝計佯敗，取計佯與，
translation_en: …then nothing is better than having the regional defense officials themselves recommend men they know, and having the Minister of War appoint them according to their suitability. If the regional defense officials obtain good generals, they have support in the field; if the Minister of War obtains good generals, he has men to rely upon from within the court. There would then scarcely be cause to worry about the means of subduing the enemy. Even so, these two officials—the Minister of War and the regional defense official—are especially important. Their particular importance makes their careful selection all the more necessary. Thus, when the Son of Heaven selects a Minister of War at court, he entrusts the office only to someone with discernment; when he selects a regional defense official outside the capital, he likewise entrusts the office only to someone with discernment. When these two officials come forward in response to their selection, the one at court assesses a man's abilities and dares not recommend him unless he can discharge the duties; the one in the field assesses the circumstances and dares not appoint him unless he can manage them. If selection above is exacting and assessment below is also thorough, capable men will hold authority. When capable men hold authority, there is no case in which the frontiers are insecure. If someone whose strengths lie elsewhere is entrusted with the direction of military affairs, he is being employed beyond his competence. How could one employ him beyond his competence and yet demand that the frontiers necessarily be secure? Thus, for these two officials, discernment comes first; those without it must not be entrusted with office. Wang Gongxiang and Ma Duansu both excelled in discernment. Unless their discernment is recognized, their plans will not be employed. Hence, when a state possesses men of discernment, it must also value the ability to recognize such men. Why is this? A plan for a hundred years cannot produce results immediately, yet those who see only what lies before their eyes call it impractical. A plan perceived by one man alone cannot be made apparent to everyone, yet those who fail to grasp its intent call it deceitful. A cautious plan seems timid; a plan that responds promptly to the occasion seems rash. A plan for victory feigns defeat; a plan for taking feigns giving…
